points: When Jeremiah finished speaking all the words of the Most High, Azariah the son of Hoshaiah, Johanan the son of Kareah, and all the proud men told him he spoke falsely and called him a lying prophet; pride is destruction according to the scriptures.

note.label: Jeremiah 43: The Proud Men Reject the Word and Flee to Egypt

points: They accused Baruch the son of Neriah of setting Jeremiah against them to deliver them into the hand of the Chaldeans, to be put to death or carried captive to Babylon.

note.label: Jeremiah 43: The Proud Men Reject the Word and Flee to Egypt

points: Many people ask for counsel while already having their own minds made up; when the counsel is not what they want to hear they go looking for someone who will tell them what they want, and so these men obeyed not the voice of the Most High to dwell in Judah.

note.label: Jeremiah 43: The Proud Men Reject the Word and Flee to Egypt

points: Johanan and all the captains took the whole remnant of Judah, the men, women, children, and the king's daughters that Nebuzaradan had left with Gedaliah, along with Jeremiah the prophet and Baruch.

note.label: Jeremiah 43: The Proud Men Reject the Word and Flee to Egypt

points: They came into the land of Egypt as far as Tahpanhes because they obeyed not the voice of the Most High.

note.label: Jeremiah 43: The Proud Men Reject the Word and Flee to Egypt

points: The word of the Most High came to Jeremiah in Tahpanhes to take great stones and hide them in the clay of the brick kiln at the entry of Pharaoh's house, in the sight of the men of Judah.

note.label: Jeremiah 43: The Proud Men Reject the Word and Flee to Egypt

points: The Most High declared He would send for Nebuchadnezzar the king of Babylon, His servant, set his throne upon those hidden stones, spread his royal pavilion over them, and smite the land of Egypt.

note.label: Jeremiah 43: The Proud Men Reject the Word and Flee to Egypt

points: When Nebuchadnezzar came he would deliver such as were for death to death, such as were for captivity to captivity, and such as were for the sword to the sword; in war each person already has an appointed end that the Most High has set.

note.label: Jeremiah 43: The Proud Men Reject the Word and Flee to Egypt

points: He would kindle a fire in the houses of the gods of Egypt, array himself with the land of Egypt as a shepherd puts on his garment so that none escape, break the images of Bethshemesh, and burn the houses of the gods of the Egyptians with fire.
